distractor_logic: This multiplies \( I \) by \( e \) instead of dividing.
The power of ten was handled wrongly when dividing by \( 10^{-19} \).
The ratio was inverted in the mantissa, giving 5 instead of 2.

questions.chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Electron Emission and the Photoelectric Effect: Experimental Observations and Laws
questions.question: Very dim light of frequency above the threshold falls on a metal. Compared with bright light of the same frequency, which statement is correct?
options: Emission begins only after the metal has absorbed enough energy, but the maximum kinetic energy is the same
Emission still begins instantly and the maximum kinetic energy is the same; only fewer electrons are emitted
Emission begins instantly but the maximum kinetic energy is smaller
No emission occurs because the light is too dim
questions.explanation:
Each photon interacts with a single electron at once, so there is no build-up time, even for dim light.

The photon energy \( hf \) is the same as in bright light, so \( KE_{max} \) is the same; dim light only means fewer photons, hence fewer electrons.
questions.hint: Dim light is fewer photons, not weaker photons.
distractor_logic: The accumulation-time idea comes from wave theory and is contradicted by experiment.
Intensity does not affect maximum kinetic energy, in either direction.
Above-threshold light always causes emission, however dim.

questions.chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation, Work Function, and Threshold Frequency
questions.question: For a metal, the stopping potential is 0.414 V at \( f=6\times10^{14} \) Hz and 2.07 V at \( f=10\times10^{14} \) Hz. What is the threshold frequency \( f_0 \)?
questions.hint: Extend the straight line down to \( V_0=0 \).
distractor_logic: This is just the first data point, where \( V_0 \) is not zero.
The correction was applied in the wrong direction (subtracted twice).
This is the second data point, where \( V_0 \) is largest.

questions.chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation, Work Function, and Threshold Frequency
questions.question: The \( V_0 \)-versus-\( f \) line of metal A has slope \( 4.14\times10^{-15} \) V s and \( f_0=5\times10^{14} \) Hz. Metal B has a larger work function. What does B's line look like?
options: A steeper slope, but the same threshold frequency
A smaller slope, and a threshold frequency above \( 5\times10^{14} \) Hz
Same slope, and it cuts the frequency axis below \( 5\times10^{14} \) Hz
Same slope \( 4.14\times10^{-15} \) V s, but it cuts the frequency axis at a frequency above \( 5\times10^{14} \) Hz
questions.explanation:
The slope is \( h/e \), identical for every metal.

A larger \( \phi \) means a larger \( f_0=\phi/h \), so B's line is shifted to the right, parallel to A's.
questions.hint: Slope depends only on universal constants.
distractor_logic: The slope never depends on the metal; only the intercept does.
A different slope contradicts \( h/e \) being universal.
Larger \( \phi \) raises \( f_0 \); it cannot move the intercept lower.

questions.chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation, Work Function, and Threshold Frequency
questions.question: A \( V_0 \)-versus-\( f \) line for a metal, when extended backwards, meets the \( V_0 \)-axis at \( -2.3 \) V. What does this intercept represent, and what is the work function?
options: It equals \( h/e \), so \( h \) can be read directly from it
It equals the threshold frequency \( f_0 \), so \( f_0=2.3 \) Hz
questions.explanation:
\( V_0=\dfrac{h}{e}f-\dfrac{\phi}{e} \). Setting \( f=0 \) gives the \( V_0 \)-intercept \( -\phi/e \).

\( -\phi/e=-2.3 \) V, so \( \phi=2.3 \) eV (sodium-like).
questions.hint: Put \( f=0 \) into the \( V_0 \) equation.
distractor_logic: \( h/e \) is the slope, not an intercept.
The minus sign belongs to the intercept; work function is positive.
\( f_0 \) is the intercept on the frequency axis, not the \( V_0 \)-axis.

questions.chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation, Work Function, and Threshold Frequency
questions.question: The same metal is illuminated first by 414 nm light and then by 248.4 nm light. By how much does the stopping potential increase? (The work function is not given.) (Take \( h=4.14\times10^{-15} \) eV s and \( c=3\times10^{8} \) m/s, so \( hc=1242 \) eV nm.)
options: It cannot be found without the work function
questions.explanation:
Photon energies: \( \dfrac{1242}{414}=3 \) eV and \( \dfrac{1242}{248.4}=5 \) eV.

\( eV_2-eV_1=(5-\phi)-(3-\phi)=2 \) eV, so the stopping potential rises by 2 V; \( \phi \) cancels.
questions.hint: Write both Einstein equations and subtract.
distractor_logic: This adds the photon energies instead of subtracting.
\( \phi \) cancels in the difference, so it is not needed.
This is the ratio of photon energies, not the difference.

questions.chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation, Work Function, and Threshold Frequency
questions.question: A metal has threshold wavelength \( \lambda_0=621 \) nm. It is illuminated with light of wavelength \( \lambda_{light}=414 \) nm. What is the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons? (Take \( h=4.14\times10^{-15} \) eV s and \( c=3\times10^{8} \) m/s, so \( hc=1242 \) eV nm.)
options: 0 eV, since the work function equals the photon energy
questions.explanation:
\( \phi=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}=\dfrac{1242}{621}=2 \) eV (using the threshold wavelength).

Photon energy \( =\dfrac{1242}{414}=3 \) eV, so \( KE_{max}=3-2=1 \) eV.
questions.hint: Use \( \lambda_0 \) for the work function and \( \lambda_{light} \) for the photon.
distractor_logic: This computes \( \phi \) from the incident 414 nm wavelength instead of \( \lambda_0 \).
The two energies were added instead of subtracted.
This is \( \phi \), not the kinetic energy.

questions.chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation, Work Function, and Threshold Frequency
questions.question: When light of frequency \( f \) falls on a metal, \( KE_{max}=1 \) eV. When the frequency is \( 2f \), \( KE_{max}=4 \) eV. What is the work function?
questions.explanation:
\( hf-\phi=1 \) and \( 2hf-\phi=4 \).

Subtracting: \( hf=3 \) eV, so \( \phi=3-1=2 \) eV.
questions.hint: Two equations, two unknowns: \( hf \) and \( \phi \).
distractor_logic: This assumes \( \phi \) equals the first kinetic energy.
This is \( hf \), not \( \phi \).
Half of the first kinetic energy has no basis.

questions.chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photon: Energy, Momentum, and the Particle Nature of Light
questions.question: A 3 mW beam of 663 nm light (photon momentum \( 1\times10^{-27} \) kg m/s, \( 1\times10^{16} \) photons per second) is completely absorbed by a surface. What force does it exert?
questions.explanation:
Force equals momentum delivered per second: \( F=np \).

\( F=1\times10^{16}\times1\times10^{-27}=1\times10^{-11} \) N.
questions.hint: Force is the rate of change of momentum.
distractor_logic: Doubling applies to perfect reflection, not absorption.
This is the momentum of one photon, not the rate for the whole beam.
This is the power in watts, not a force.

questions.chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photon: Energy, Momentum, and the Particle Nature of Light
questions.question: Photon X has wavelength 331.5 nm and photon Y has wavelength 663 nm. Which quantity is the same for both?
options: The ratio \( E/p \), which equals \( c \)
questions.explanation:
For any photon, \( E=pc \), so \( E/p=c \) always.

X has twice the energy and twice the momentum of Y, but the ratio is the same.
questions.hint: Look for a combination that removes the wavelength.
distractor_logic: X's shorter wavelength gives it twice the energy.
X's shorter wavelength gives it twice the momentum.
\( f=c/\lambda_{light} \), so X has twice the frequency of Y.

questions.chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photon: Energy, Momentum, and the Particle Nature of Light
questions.question: A photon has momentum \( 2.21\times10^{-27} \) kg m/s. What is its frequency? (Take \( h=6.63\times10^{-34} \) J s and \( c=3\times10^{8} \) m/s.)
questions.hint: Convert momentum to energy first, then energy to frequency.
distractor_logic: This is \( h/p \), the wavelength in metres, not a frequency.
This is the energy \( pc \); the division by \( h \) was skipped.
The final ratio was inverted.

questions.chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photon: Energy, Momentum, and the Particle Nature of Light
questions.question: A source emits power \( P \) at frequency \( f \). If the frequency is doubled but the power is kept the same, the number of photons emitted per second:
options: Doubles, since frequency counts photons per second
Stays the same, since power is unchanged
Halves, since each photon now carries twice the energy
questions.explanation:
Photons per second \( =\dfrac{P}{hf} \).

Doubling \( f \) at fixed \( P \) halves the number of photons per second.
questions.hint: Power is shared among photons of energy \( hf \).
distractor_logic: Frequency is the wave's oscillation rate, not the photon emission rate.
Same power but more energy per photon means fewer photons.
The dependence on \( f \) is inverse, not inverse-square.

questions.chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photon: Energy, Momentum, and the Particle Nature of Light
questions.question: Which statement best describes the dual nature of light?
options: Light shows wave behaviour in propagation (interference, diffraction) and particle behaviour when it exchanges energy with matter (photoelectric effect)
Light is a wave in vacuum and a particle only inside materials
Light is a particle at high intensity and a wave at low intensity
Light is a wave at low frequency and a particle only at high frequency
questions.explanation:
Interference and diffraction need a wave description.

Absorption and emission, as in the photoelectric effect, occur in whole photons. Both pictures are needed, depending on the phenomenon.
questions.hint: Which kinds of experiment reveal each behaviour?
distractor_logic: Photons are particles in vacuum too; the medium is not the deciding factor.
Intensity changes photon number, not which nature light shows.
Even low-frequency light is absorbed in photons.

questions.chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photon: Energy, Momentum, and the Particle Nature of Light
questions.question: How many photons of energy 2 eV together carry a total energy of 1 J? (Take \( 1 \) eV \( =1.6\times10^{-19} \) J.)
questions.explanation:
One photon: \( 2\times1.6\times10^{-19}=3.2\times10^{-19} \) J.

Number \( =\dfrac{1}{3.2\times10^{-19}}=3.125\times10^{18} \).
questions.hint: Convert the photon energy to joules first.
distractor_logic: This is the energy of one photon, not the number of photons.
This uses 1 eV per photon instead of 2 eV.
This divides 1 J by 2 eV without converting eV to joules.

questions.chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: De Broglie Wavelength and the Wave Nature of Matter
questions.question: A proton and an alpha particle are accelerated from rest through the same potential difference. Find the ratio \( \lambda_p/\lambda_\alpha \) of their de Broglie wavelengths. (Take \( m_\alpha=4m_p \) and \( q_\alpha=2q_p \).)
questions.explanation:
\( \lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}} \), so \( \dfrac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_\alpha}=\sqrt{\dfrac{m_\alpha q_\alpha}{m_pq_p}} \).

\( =\sqrt{4\times2}=\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt{2} \). The lighter proton has the longer wavelength.
questions.hint: Both mass and charge differ; include both under the root.
distractor_logic: This inverts the ratio, giving the heavier alpha the larger wavelength.
The square root was forgotten.
Only the mass ratio was used; the charge ratio was ignored.

questions.chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: De Broglie Wavelength and the Wave Nature of Matter
questions.question: A neutron of mass \( 1.6\times10^{-27} \) kg has kinetic energy \( 2\times10^{-20} \) J. What is its de Broglie wavelength? (Take \( h=6.63\times10^{-34} \) J s.)
